title: Seeds on the Balcony
passage:
When Yuta's family moved to an apartment, he missed the small garden beside their old house. The new home had no yard, only a narrow balcony that received morning sunlight. Yuta assumed that growing vegetables would no longer be possible. His mother suggested trying a few pots before giving up.

They began with lettuce, radishes, and small tomatoes. Yuta filled containers with soil and carefully followed the instructions on the seed packets. During the first week, nothing seemed to happen. He checked the pots every morning and wondered whether the seeds were bad. Then tiny green leaves appeared. They were so small that he almost missed them.

The balcony created new problems. Wind dried the soil faster than it had in the old garden, and one container received too much water during heavy rain. The tomato plant also leaned toward the railing because it was searching for sunlight. Yuta and his mother moved the pots, added simple supports, and made small holes so extra water could escape. They discovered that growing plants in a limited space required different methods, not less care.

By early summer, they could pick lettuce for sandwiches and several red radishes. The tomatoes took longer. Yuta became impatient because the green fruit seemed unchanged for days. His mother told him that checking every hour would not make them ripen faster. When the first tomato finally turned red, he waited one extra day before picking it. The taste was not especially different from tomatoes sold in a store, but he felt proud because he knew every step that had brought it to the plate.

The balcony never became a real garden in the old sense. There was no grass, no tree, and not enough space to grow many plants. Yet Yuta stopped thinking of it as a poor replacement. It was simply a different kind of growing place. He learned that losing one condition does not always mean losing the activity itself. Sometimes the activity can survive if people are willing to change the way they do it.
translation:
ユウタの家族が集合住宅へ引っ越したとき、彼は以前の家の横にあった小さな庭が恋しくなりました。新居には庭がなく、朝日が当たる細いベランダしかありません。野菜作りはもうできないと思っていましたが、母は諦める前に鉢で試してみようと提案しました。

レタス、ラディッシュ、ミニトマトから始め、種袋の説明をよく読んで植えました。一週目は何も起きないように見えましたが、やがて見落としそうなほど小さな緑の芽が出ました。

ベランダには庭とは違う問題がありました。風で土が早く乾き、大雨では水がたまり、トマトは日光を求めて手すり側へ傾きました。鉢の位置を変え、支柱を立て、余分な水が抜ける穴を作ることで対応しました。狭い場所では世話が少なくなるのではなく、方法が変わるのだと分かりました。

初夏にはサンドイッチ用のレタスや赤いラディッシュを収穫できました。トマトは時間がかかり、ユウタは待ちきれませんでしたが、母から何度見ても早く熟すわけではないと言われました。最初の実が赤くなったとき、あえてもう一日待ってから取りました。店のトマトと特別違う味ではありませんでしたが、皿に届くまでのすべての過程を知っていることが誇らしく感じられました。

ベランダは昔の庭と同じにはなりませんでした。芝生も木もなく、多くの植物を育てる広さもありません。それでもユウタは『劣った代用品』とは考えなくなりました。条件が一つ失われても、やり方を変えれば活動そのものは続けられることがあると学んだのです。
